title: Lettre Tate (mai 66) (Cristaux) : lettre (1966), tapuscrit (s.d.), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is a very faint first draft of the 'Compléments sur les groupes de Witt' that is recopied more legibly on the next page (69). The two pages match closely line by line, so the faint text can be read through p.69.

Setting: S = Spec A of characteristic p. G_a is the additive group and W_n the Witt vectors of length n. Ext^1 denotes the sheaf Ext of commutative group schemes (fppf).

Lemma 1. Ext^1(G_a, G_a) is the free A-module on the classes F^i e. Equivalently it is the free (left) A[F]-module generated by e, where e is the class of W_2 viewed as an extension 0 -> G_a -> W_2 -> G_a -> 0. Here e is the Witt cocycle (x^p + y^p - (x+y)^p)/p.
- Proof idea: reduce by a limit argument to A = F_p.
- Then cite Demazure-Gabriel II §3 4.6.

Lemma 2. Let H be a subgroup scheme of G_a that locally on S looks like a kernel of an additive map with G_a/H locally isomorphic to G_a (e.g. α_{p^m} or the kernel of an additive polynomial). Then:
- (o) Ext^1(H, W_n) -> Ext^1(H, W_1) is bijective.
- (a1) Ext^1(H, W_{n-1}) -> Ext^1(H, W_n) is zero; equivalently a connecting map from a Hom-term into Ext^1(H, W_{n-1}) is surjective.
- (a2) Ext^1(H, W_1) -> Ext^1(H, W_{n-1}) is zero.
- (b) Restriction Ext^1(G_a, W_n) -> Ext^1(H, W_n) is surjective, i.e. Ext^1(H, W_n) -> Ext^2(G_a/H, W_n) vanishes.
- (c) Ext^1(G_a, W_n) is generated as a (right) A[F]-module by the class of W_{n+1}, viewed as an extension of G_a by W_n.

Proof sketch (fuller on p.69):
- For n = 1, (b) follows from local vanishing of Ext^2(G_a, G_a), and (c) is Lemma 1.
- General n goes by induction on n via the sequences 0 -> W_{n-1} -> W_n -> W_1 -> 0.

Purpose: in the context of the 1966 Tate letter on crystals and Dieudonné theory, these lemmas compute Ext(H, W_n) for finite subgroups of G_a over general bases. This is the kind of input needed to define and compute Dieudonné modules of finite group schemes over a base as Ext^1(G, W_n) (or Ext into the crystalline structure sheaf), and to check exactness and base change on test objects such as α_p.
errors: Lemma 1's reduction 'par limite' to A = F_p implicitly uses that the cocycle description of Ext^1(G_a, G_a) is compatible with base change (G_a flat, Lazard's symmetric cocycles defined over Z). This is true but not argued.

The left/right A[F]-module conventions are juggled: Lemma 1 has 'à gauche', Lemma 2(c) has 'droite'. They are reconciled only because F∘e = e∘F for the Witt cocycle with F_p coefficients; this is not stated.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a faint, superseded draft of p.69. It contains standard lemmas on Ext of G_a and its subgroups by Witt groups, already in Demazure-Gabriel. The only mild point is working over a general base S, but this is routine.
transcription_corrections: Title: should read 'Compléments sur les groupes de Witt', not 'groupes W(k)'.
Lemma 1 begins 'Soit S = Spec(A) de car. p' (as on p.69), not 'k parfait'.
Read 'Ext^1(G_a, G_a)' instead of 'Ext^1(G_1, G_2)', and 'A[F]-module' instead of 'A(k)-module'.
Read 'engendré par les F^i e ... e est la classe de W_2 considéré comme extension de G_a par G_a'.
Proof line: 'Dém. On peut supposer par limite que A = F_p ... Demazure-Gabriel II §3 4.6'.
Lemma 2: 'Soit H un sous-schéma en groupes de G_a, tel que ... G_a/H soit loc. isomorphe à G_a'. G_1 in the machine transcription should be G_a throughout.
Items a), b), c) correspond to o)/a1)/a2), b), c) on p.69. Item c) reads 'Ext^1(G_a, W_n) est un A[F]-module engendré par la classe de W_{n+1}'.
